approach: Three parts inside the existing mechanical-revision flow, so no critic round is used. (1) admission.rs: `open_questions_findings` gets a third `else if` branch calling a new helper `asks_about_existing_behavior`. The helper strips the User:/Host: prefix first, so its exemptions apply to the body only. It gives a major finding at "open questions" when a prefixed question asks whether existing tests break, or what a backticked named function does on its failure or retry path. Exemptions: a body whose first word is should/shall/would, a body containing acceptable/allowed/prefer(s)/wish, `user` followed by want/expect/prefer, or a host-environment word (toolchain, platform, machine, os, host). (2) planner.md: an exact byte ledger with net change 0, so the file stays 2383 bytes and the planner budget line (1105 in docs/system-facts.md) is unchanged. (3) Tests: admission.rs unit tests, refusal_corpus.rs cases, and a job_plan.rs test that drives the scripted planner/critic Scenario. planning.rs gets a comment only. fake.rs stays unchanged on purpose.

decisions.choice: Put the rule in `open_questions_findings` as a third `else if` branch (after has_addressee and says_code_answers, admission.rs:528-544) calling a new helper `asks_about_existing_behavior`. At most one finding per question. An unprefixed test-breakage question keeps its 'no addressee' finding.
decisions.reason: Existing tests count one finding per question (admission.rs:1179-1203; `question_findings` in refusal_corpus.rs expects exactly one). The only production caller chain is plan_findings (admission.rs:314) <- planning.rs:217. Its major findings return `RoundEnd::Mechanical` before `critic_round`, so no critic round is used.

rejected.option: A new top-level scan in plan_findings over open questions, risks and steps
rejected.why: It widens the false-refusal surface to prose that is not an open question and can double-count a question the addressee rule already refuses.

rejected.option: Change MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES or add a RoundEnd variant
rejected.why: Out of scope; the mechanical path already does not use the round.

decisions.choice: The helper lowercases the question, trims leading whitespace, `*`, `_` and backticks (the same trim as has_addressee, admission.rs:551-556), removes the `user:` or `host:` prefix, trims again, and tokenizes only the body (split on non-alphanumerics). Every exemption is checked on the body tokens, never on the prefix.
decisions.reason: Earlier critic finding: the prefix token 'host' made every Host: question exempt, contradicting criterion 2 ('even with a User: or Host: prefix'). Unit assertions pin that 'Host: which other tests fail if the budget line changes?' is refused and 'Host: do existing tests fail on the production host's older toolchain?' is accepted (body tokens host and toolchain).

rejected.option: Drop bare 'host' from the exemption list and keep toolchain/platform/machine/os
rejected.why: 'does the host's cargo fail existing tests' would be refused; stripping the prefix is the exact fix and keeps 'host' meaningful in the body.

rejected.option: Pin the Host: toolchain question in the corpus as a known false positive
rejected.why: A refused host question cannot be answered by the planner at all.

decisions.choice: Narrow the decision exemption to forms that mark a decision: (a) the first body token is should, shall or would; (b) any body token is acceptable, allowed, prefer, prefers or wish; (c) adjacent tokens `user` + want|wants|expect|expects|prefer. 'may', 'expect' and 'want' alone do not exempt. Pinned refuse cases: 'User: do existing tests that expect the old wording break?' and 'User: may existing tests fail after this?'. The doc comment lists the remaining known miss: a breakage question phrased 'should existing tests ...' or naming a platform/toolchain is not refused.
decisions.reason: The tokens 'expect' and 'may' appear in plain code-fact questions. Accept cases that matter stay accepted: 'User: should other tests that fail be skipped?' (first token should), 'User: what does the user expect `athena land` to print on failure?' (user + expect), 'User: may the change edit tests in `crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs`?' (no existing/other + tests pair, so it never matches).

rejected.option: Keep the flat list {should, may, prefer, want, expect, wish, allowed, acceptable} anywhere in the body
rejected.why: Exempts 'do existing tests that expect the old wording break?' and 'may existing tests fail after this?' (critic finding 4 of an earlier round).

decisions.choice: Match test-breakage as an adjacent token pair (existing|other, test|tests) or (tests, outside), AND a token in {break, breaks, broken, breakage, fail, fails, failing, failure, failures, regress, regresses, regression}. Match the function form as a backticked span (odd-indexed segment of body.split('`') that has a closing backtick; identifier characters alphanumeric, `_`, `:`, optional trailing `()`; no space, `/` or `.`) AND one of 'what does', 'what happens', 'how does' AND one of 'failure path', 'retry path', 'on failure', 'on retry', 'on error', 'when it fails', 'if it fails'.
decisions.reason: Narrow and searchable. Paths such as `crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs` give the token 'tests' but never a pair with existing/other/outside, so the scope questions accepted at admission.rs:1225-1229 and refusal_corpus.rs (user-scope-question-citing-a-path) still pass.

rejected.option: Refuse any prefixed question containing 'test' or 'which'/'any'/'current'
rejected.why: Refuses real decisions and scope questions (admission.rs:1226).

rejected.option: Refuse 'what does' plus a backticked name without a failure phrase
rejected.why: 'User: what does the user expect `athena land` to print?' is a decision, not a code fact.

risks.risk: The wording match refuses a genuine User: or Host: decision.
risks.mitigation: The rule needs an adjacent existing|other + test(s) (or tests + outside) pair with a break/fail word, or a backticked function name with 'what does/happens/how does' and a failure/retry phrase. Exemptions on the body: first word should/shall/would; acceptable, allowed, prefer(s), wish; `user` + want/expect/prefer; toolchain, platform, machine, os, host. Counterexamples are pinned as accept cases in admission.rs and the corpus. A refused planner rewords and loses one mechanical pass, not a critic round.

risks.risk: The check misses rewordings: 'does the suite still pass?', a question avoiding 'test', a function named without backticks, a breakage question phrased 'should existing tests ...', or one that names a platform or toolchain.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment lists these known misses, as `risks_findings` does at admission.rs:332-337. The planner brief bullet and the critic cover them. Proving a function claim true is out of scope.

risks.risk: The planner.md byte ledger is off by a few bytes, moving the composed size to another ceil(bytes/3) bucket and failing the budgets test or the 800-token cap.
risks.mitigation: The ledger was counted per edited string from the Read of the file (49 -> 193, 26 -> 145 plus 34, -276, -21 = 0). The step has the producer run `ls -l` (target 2383 bytes) before the tests. If the size differs, the producer pads or trims only the new line 5 wording or the merged line 8 wording by the exact difference and reruns the budgets test, which names the computed value. It does not edit docs/system-facts.md or any other frame.

The changelog and doc comment say about 3% of newly refused plans, labelled an estimate from the reading, not a measurement. The higher refusal rate is intended, because those plans spent critic rounds on impact the planner can find by searching. A plan that keeps asking stops after MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES (planning.rs:486), as for any major finding.
